newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMU woes seen trapping German shares in range.
newsitem.headline: EMU woes seen trapping German shares in range.

text.p: A myriad of worries about the future for monetary union and the domestic political outlook should keep German shares rangebound for the time being, albeit close to record highs, dealers said on Wednesday.
"Fundamentally, the trend still seems to be upward but we will have to wait a while before the party starts again," said a Frankfurt dealer.

"If the euro project is derailed, we will have some extremely confused markets. Until we have some clarity on monetary union, some clear confirmation that it will go ahead, the EMU story will remain a negative factor," he added.
The IBIS DAX index was down one point at 3,670.16 points at 1313 GMT, some seven points below the DAX index closing level in mid-afternoon.
Dealers said while the strong overnight performance on Wall Street, the stable dollar and reasonably steady Bund market had supported the market through the day, caution was still prevailing.

Some investors had already closed their books before the end of the first half-year of 1997, one dealer noted, while others said the forthcoming DAX options expiry next week on the DTB futures and options exchange was holding the market back.
But the risk on the downside was not too great, according to many dealers.
The fundamental earnings outlook for German corporations was still positive and the risk of interest rate hikes in Germany was still minimal, given modest growth.

The projected range for the DAX, at least until the Amsterdam Summit next week which is expected to clarify key monetary union questions, was between 3,630 and 3,750 points, according to one leading bank.
The IBIS DAX index hit an alltime high of 3,734.05 points on Monday.

While the broad market was flat, individual shares were moving dramatically, most notably retailer Karstadt AG which has been rising amid persistent rumours that WCM, a German holding company, is planning to buy a major stake in it from German banks.
WCM has consistently denied this, but dealers say banks' cautious responses to the rumours have been interpreted as confirmation that the story is true.
Karstadt was up 23 marks, or nearly four percent, at 648 marks in afternoon trade, having traded on relatively high volumes through the day.
Airline Deutsche Lufthansa was markedly weak, trading down 54 pfennigs at 30.50 marks.
Dealers said the move was due to profit-taking.
"This is getting to be a very selective market," commented one dealer.
